research.text:
DEEP RESEARCH (browser bot, read the pages itself):
- Grace Hopper invented the first compiler, called A-0, in 1952 while working on the UNIVAC I at Eckert-Mauchly Computer Corporation (https://www.computerhistory.org/tdih/august/16/).
- Before Hopper's compiler, programmers had to write instructions entirely in numeric machine code or cumbersome assembly language (https://www.britannica.com/technology/compiler-computer-science).
- Hopper famously stated that humans are allergic to change and kept telling her that computers could only do arithmetic, not understand English words (https://history.aip.org/history/exhibits/hopper/ftf4.htm).
- The A-0 compiler translated mathematical notation and English-like pseudocode into machine-readable binary code (https://spectrum.ieee.org/grace-hopper-compiler).
- Hopper wanted to make programming accessible to non-mathematicians and business people who didn't know binary (https://www.womenshistory.org/education-resources/biographies/grace-hopper).
- Her pioneering work directly led to the creation of COBOL in 1959, one of the first high-level programming languages (https://www.nsa.gov/portals/75/documents/news-features/declassified-documents/tech-journals/grace-hopper.pdf).
- Hopper earned the nickname "Amazing Grace" and rose to the rank of Rear Admiral in the United States Navy (https://www.defensenc.mil/News/News-Stories/Article/Article/2198083/rear-admiral-grace-m-hopper-amazing-grace/).
- Despite creating the breakthrough tool that spawned all modern software development, Hopper's original A-0 system predated modern keyboard-based coding environments, operating largely via punch cards (https://americanhistory.si.edu/collections/search/object/nmah_334547).

HOOK IDEAS:
1. The person who invented software coding didn't actually write a single line of code.
2. Meet the woman who invented the compiler—even though everyone told her computers could only do math.
